video_title: What's Next For New-Look Charlotte Hornets? w/ Moussa Diabaté

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on the new team chemistry and energy
quotes.excerpt: Obviously we got some new guys. I think it's a different vibe, different energy, but it's been great.
quotes.quote: Obviously we got some new guys. I think it's a different vibe, different energy, but it's been great.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on the coaching staff's focus on team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: As a coaching staff it's been a very big part that they wanted to emphasize on.
quotes.quote: As a coaching staff it's been a very big part that they wanted to emphasize on. Obviously because we have a whole lot of different players. A lot of exercise based on getting to know each other, whether it's on the court or off the court, different activities that we can do just so we can build that chemistry and really create that relationship.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his relationship with head coach Charles Lee
quotes.excerpt: There's not a lot of times that you'll see a two-way guy play this many games.
quotes.quote: First thing is I'll always be grateful to him because he gave me the opportunity coming in. There's not a lot of times that you'll see a two-way guy play this many games. I think I ended up having the most games when I came in, so I'm always going to be forever grateful for that.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté compares coaching styles of Charles Lee and Ty Lue
quotes.excerpt: Ty Lue was a lot more laid back. Charles Lee is a lot more energetic.
quotes.quote: If I'm coming back from when I was back with the Clippers with Ty Lue, there is a little difference. But at the end of the day, it just all depends on who the person is, whether they're young or not. For example, Ty Lue was a lot more laid back. Charles Lee is a lot more energetic. He's a lot more out there. So there's different ways to coach, but great either way.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his early basketball motivation
quotes.excerpt: The first thing I can remember that really made me like basketball was seeing progress.
quotes.quote: The first thing I can remember that really made me like basketball was seeing progress. Not more so playing well, but just knowing that coach told me something and I was able to apply it and now I can do it. Just learning how to do a layup, oh now I can do a layup. Just the understanding of being able to get better was what I got addicted to.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on playing fast in the Hornets' system
quotes.excerpt: Playing fast is my motto. I'm not as good or as efficient playing the half-court slow game.
quotes.quote: Playing fast is my motto. I'm not as good or as efficient playing the half-court slow game. I like to run. We shoot a bunch of threes, I'm coming in for the offensive rebound, whatever it is, high screens, just trying to get downhill and trying to play fast. I think for me that's the best way to play.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his defensive movement and impact
quotes.excerpt: I'm putting myself in the position where I feel like I'm more dynamic and he has to follow me.
quotes.quote: When I'm guarding a big man, in my mind, I don't more so think of defense on a big man, but I also think that me playing offense and being able to move also plays some type of defense on the other big man. When you don't move, the big man gets a lot more chance to rest. At the moment, I'm able to make him move as much as I can. I'm putting myself in the position where I feel like I'm more dynamic and he has to follow me.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his development as a screener
quotes.excerpt: Just the way you want to come into the screen, whether you want to come fast or slow.
quotes.quote: We've talked about it a lot, just coming in from the angles, different situations, just the way you want to come into the screen, whether you want to come fast or slow, you want to stay into the screen, just being able to read the big man. There's so many reads that comes into it, but overall it's been a lot of progression.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on different ways to play the screen
quotes.excerpt: They all have different ways that they want to play the screen.
quotes.quote: They all have different ways that they want to play the screen. Some might want to keep it and try to play the pocket. Some might want me to stick it so they can snake, which means come to the other side and play that little in-the-middle mid-range game. Some of them might just want you to not even set the screen, just act like you're going to set the screen and just turn the corner to the basket.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his approach to offensive rebounding
quotes.excerpt: I wouldn't say I have a technique. I'm just trying to go for the ball.
quotes.quote: I wouldn't say I have a technique. I'm just trying to go for the ball and trying to get there before the other person does. I wouldn't say I have a technique, maybe I should look at one, looking at different things I could do, but I'm just trying to get to the ball no matter what.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his growth as a self-creator
quotes.excerpt: Every big doesn't want to start dribbling and stuff, but for me I want to keep the main thing.
quotes.quote: Every big doesn't want to start dribbling and stuff, but for me I want to keep the main thing, the main thing. Keep the bread and butter. Don't forget that while also being able to build up that foundation. Being able to use more responsibility into my playmaking, find different situations where I can be more effective on offense, I think it's going to be a very big part.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his perimeter defensive rating
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to keep it humble. I'm going to say like an eight.
quotes.quote: I'm going to keep it humble. I'm going to say like an eight. I think it's cool, I think I'm pretty good. I'll just say there's also times when I feel like you have a certain gift or something, you tend to try to play a little more lazy. For example, sometimes I open up naturally just so I can get the block. Sometimes you just got to stick to the fundamentals, stay in front of the ball, and just play that way.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on the importance of summer training
quotes.excerpt: I'll give credit big time to my summers. I naturally have a lot heavier load in my workouts.
quotes.quote: I'll give credit big time to my summers. I naturally have a lot heavier load in my workouts than most people. Just level of intensity. I try to have very intense summers which lead to like me, comes to conditioning or anything like that. I feel like I tend to be able to do more just naturally. I think it really comes down to my summer, just whether it's in the weight room or on the basketball court, just really just make it very intense for myself.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his off-season development goals
quotes.excerpt: Get stronger, get more explosive, be as athletic as I can be.
quotes.quote: Get stronger, get more explosive, be as athletic as I can be. And then on the court, I mean really just whether it's coming from playmaking, touch around the rim, different moves that I can work on, different situation I can work on, just all those things combined really.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his hobbies outside of basketball
quotes.excerpt: I love to talk to my family. I love going on drives and play video games.
quotes.quote: I love to talk to my family. I love going on drives and play video games. Really those are the main things that I'll do and yeah just get off my feet.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his favorite anime
quotes.excerpt: All time probably Naruto. Right now, the best one I've watched recently, I'd say Clevedies.
quotes.quote: All time probably Naruto. Right now, the best one I've watched recently, I'd say Clevedies. Clevedies was a very good one. I don't know if y'all like anime, but Clevedies is like a pretty good anime y'all should probably tap in.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabaté
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabaté on his favorite video games
quotes.excerpt: I play 2K, Assassin's Creed, Hogwarts. Really just any game that I feel like makes sense.
quotes.quote: I play 2K, Assassin's Creed, Hogwarts. Really just any game that I feel like makes sense to play for me. Far Cry, whatever.
